_comment: The Trusted Signing account, in the form CI needs.
The copy at the repository root (artifact-signing-metadata.json) is
git-ignored: it is the file a developer points at their own `az login`
session. A runner has no such file, so it needs one that is committed.
The account and profile names are not secrets; the authorisation to use
them is (an Azure federated credential trusting
repo:steeb-k/seed-sync-gtk:environment:release, see docs/ci-release.md §8).
`azure/login` authenticates with a GitHub OIDC token and then runs
`az login`, so what a runner ends up holding is an Azure CLI session -
exactly like a laptop. It does NOT set the environment that
EnvironmentCredential or WorkloadIdentityCredential read, so those stay
excluded along with everything interactive: a credential type that can
open a browser has no business in a non-interactive job, where it would
hang until the step times out.
TODO(maintainer): CodeSigningAccountName and CertificateProfileName below
are placeholders, not real values. Neither is recoverable from this
repo's history: the real artifact-signing-metadata.json was always
git-ignored (see commit 0d199c3, 'untrack signing metadata; add example
template'), and the only thing ever committed was
artifact-signing-metadata.example.json, which carries the same kind of
placeholder. Fill these in from the Azure portal (Trusted Signing
account / certificate profile) before the windows job in build.yml can
sign anything. Until then, `sign=true` fails fast at the 'Refuse to ship
unsigned' step as long as AZURE_CLIENT_ID is also unset — set that
secret last, after this file is correct, so a half-configured account
can't produce a build that looks signed but isn't.
